cases.name: Moenisha Yvette "Momo" Collins
cases.about: Her obituary said, "Moenisha was such a wonderful mother. Makayla was Moenisha’s entire world. She loved being Makayla’s mother more than anything in this world. At about 9 years old Moenisha became a member of Right Now Ministries, where she began her walk and have a personal relationship with Jesus Christ. Moenisha attended  Washington High School located in Washington, NC and received her high school diploma in 2014. Momo was best known for just being unapologetically her. She loved deep intimate conversations about life. Momo always pushed others to be the best version of themselves. Moenisha was sassy but sweet, strong yet gentle. She enjoyed being in her own space, Momo was truly an introvert who showed love in an extraordinary way. She will forever be missed by her family, friends & loved ones."
cases.narrative: Police said she was shot 5 times in her bedroom and her 10-year-old daughter found her deceased when she came home from school.

cases.name: Sabrina Finch
cases.about: Finch leaves behind four children, and she was her (disabled and paralyzed) brother’s primary caregiver. “She would do anything for anyone,” (her daughter Kali) Thaxton said. “She would give the shoes off her feet to anyone, the clothes off her back. She had the biggest heart no matter what. She had this spunky personality. She was really goofy. She was just a beautiful human being who was taken too soon.”
cases.narrative: (Her daughter Kali) Thaxton said Saturday’s altercation started over a misplaced pair of shoes. “He was high on drugs at the time and couldn’t find a pair of shoes, so he went into my (disabled and paralyzed) uncle’s room, shot my uncle, then shot my grandmother, then shot my mom in front of my grandmother,” she said. “[My grandmother] is still in shock. She watched it all. She had to hop out of a window to go and get help after she got shot.”
